output.myth: Aun cut the string because he wanted to know how far the wind went. The sky drifted off with him holding the knife, and every kite he had flown on that string went up after it. Ennu made the first of them from sailcloth and whale-rib, and when it broke loose it sailed up without a hand on it. Tavo the Gale laughed and would not give it back. Mother Hesk, at the pole, keeps count of every string, and she found one short. She has counted it every night since. Varesk is the cut kite. Its belly holds the bright sail-star, and its tail drops down toward the sea because a tail is the part the wind can hold. Fishermen tie a knot in their cords for each boat they lose, so Hesk can find them. Aun is said to fly Varesk still, slow in the dark, waiting for someone on the islands to take up the cut end and pull.
output.verse:
Aun cut the long string,
Varesk trails its tail below,
pull the end back home.
